source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: No early-papyrus witness preserves Matthew 17 within the 2nd-3rd c. CE corpus for these target verses; primary witnesses are the 4th c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus. (P45 [Chester Beatty I, 3rd c. CE] preserves portions of Mt 20-26 but not Mt 17.)
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference (where variants are documented)
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997 (vol 2); Luz Hermeneia 2001-2007 (vol 2); France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Bockmuehl, M., *This Jesus: Martyr, Lord, Messiah* (T&T Clark 1994); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra (ΙΣ, ΧΣ, ΚΣ, ΘΣ, ΠΝΑ, ΥΣ, ΠΗΡ) appear abbreviated in the uncials. The Transfiguration pericope (vv.1-9) is preserved without significant text-critical disturbance in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus; variant readings are documented per verse.

verses.text: Καὶ μεθ' ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ' ἰδίαν.
verses.translit: Kai meth' hēmeras hex paralambanei ho Iēsous ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn ton adelphon autou, kai anapherei autous eis oros hypsēlon kat' idian.
verses.notes: **MAJOR PERICOPE OPENING — THE TRANSFIGURATION (vv.1-9)**. *meth' hēmeras hex* (after six days) — Mark 9:2 parallel; Luke 9:28 reads *hōsei hēmerai oktō* (about eight days). The six-day interval may echo Exod 24:16 (the six-day cloud-cover before Moses ascends Sinai on the seventh day) — a deliberate Moses-typology marker (Davies-Allison ICC 2.694-695). Three named witnesses (Peter, James, John) — the inner-circle triad also at Gethsemane (Mt 26:37) and Jairus's daughter (Mark 5:37; Luke 8:51 — absent from Matthew's parallel). *oros hypsēlon* (a high mountain) — identification disputed: Mt Tabor (traditional, since Origen; geographically modest at ~575m and inhabited in the 1st c.) vs Mt Hermon (~2,800m, near Caesarea Philippi where 16:13 located the prior pericope; favored by modern scholarship: France NICNT 644-645). *kat' idian* (privately) — the secrecy motif foreshadowing the 17:9 silence-injunction. **HIGHEST LENS-RISK SITE OF CHAPTER 17 BEGINS HERE.**

verses.text: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς.
verses.translit: kai metemorphōthē emprosthen autōn, kai elampsen to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios, ta de himatia autou egeneto leuka hōs to phōs.
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK VERSE**. **The verb *metemorphōthē* (aorist passive of *metamorphoō* — 'was transformed / metamorphosed')** is the textual locus of the entire pericope's name. The passive voice is theologically loaded (divine passive — transformation effected by God) but does not specify agent. Matthew's distinctive additions over Mark: (a) the face shining *hōs ho hēlios* (as the sun) — explicit solar-luminosity comparison; (b) the garments *leuka hōs to phōs* (white as the light) — Mark's parallel reads 'gleaming, intensely white, as no fuller on earth could whiten' (Mk 9:3). Matthew's solar-face metaphor deliberately echoes (i) Moses's shining face descending Sinai (Exod 34:29-35 LXX *dedoxastai hē opsis tou chrōmatos tou prosōpou autou*); (ii) the eschatological-righteous shining 'as the sun' at Mt 13:43 (Matthean intra-corpus parallel); (iii) Dan 12:3 LXX (the wise shining as the brightness of the firmament) and (iv) the Son-of-Man-with-face-like-the-sun of Rev 1:16 (later but possibly tradition-historical kin). **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: the canon engages this as 'Elohim manifesting in glory' / 'the technologically-mediated luminous manifestation of the engineered messenger' (Raël, *The Book Which Tells the Truth*, on Sinai/Tabor luminosity). **LENS-RISK FLAG for the Editor**: do NOT pre-resolve toward (a) the Raëlian techno-luminosity reading, (b) the orthodox-Christian uncreated-divine-light reading (Athanasius / Palamite hesychasm), or (c) the rationalist-mythopoetic reading. Preserve the philological surface — a luminous transformation pericope with explicit Moses-Sinai typology. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 2.696-700; Luz Hermeneia 2.395-407; France NICNT 645-648.

verses.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας συλλαλοῦντες μετ' αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idou ōphthē autois Mōusēs kai Ēlias syllalountes met' autou.
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK VERSE — Moses and Elijah appearing**. The verb *ōphthē* (was seen / appeared — aorist passive of *horaō*) is the LXX-standard idiom for theophany / angelophany (Gen 12:7; 17:1; 18:1; Exod 3:2 etc.). Matthew gives Moses precedence; Mark 9:4 reverses the order (Elias with Moses). Standard interpretive options: (a) Moses = Law / Elijah = Prophets — the entire Hebrew canon witnessing to Jesus (Davies-Allison ICC 2.700-701); (b) both as eschatological-returning figures (Deut 18:15-18 prophet-like-Moses; Mal 4:5-6 [3:23-24 MT] Elijah-before-the-Day); (c) both as figures who experienced bodily-translation / non-ordinary departure (Deut 34:6 Moses's unknown grave; 2 Kgs 2:11 Elijah's chariot-ascension) — and thus the candidates for messianic-precursor return (cf. Rev 11:3-12 the two witnesses). **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: the canon reads Moses and Elijah as Elohim-messenger-figures present at the Tabor 'demonstration' — see Raël on Moses-as-engineered-prophet, Elijah-as-chariot-translated. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve the textual *ōphthē* + comparative-religion framing (the apparition / translated-figure motif is common across ANE prophet-traditions); do NOT pre-resolve toward (a) the Elohim-emissary reading, (b) the orthodox 'representatives of Law and Prophets' typology, or (c) any historicizing 'real Moses and Elijah' reading. Document; do not collapse.

verses.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι· εἰ θέλεις, ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
verses.translit: apokritheis de ho Petros eipen tō Iēsou· Kyrie, kalon estin hēmas hōde einai· ei theleis, poiēsō hōde treis skēnas, soi mian kai Mōusei mian kai Ēlia mian.
verses.notes: Peter's signature impulsive utterance. *skēnas* (tents / booths / tabernacles) — echoes Sukkot / Feast of Tabernacles (Lev 23:33-43); Davies-Allison (ICC 2.703-704) consider whether Peter is proposing to prolong the theophanic moment by constructing wilderness-style tabernacles for each figure. Variant: Mark 9:5 has Peter say *Rhabbi*; Luke 9:33 has *Epistata*; Matthew alone has the more reverent *Kyrie* (Lord). Matthew also has the polite conditional *ei theleis* (if you wish) — softening the Marcan 'he did not know what to say.'

verses.text: ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα· ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: eti autou lalountos idou nephelē phōteinē epeskiasen autous, kai idou phōnē ek tēs nephelēs legousa· Houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa· akouete autou.
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK VERSE — the cloud and the voice. THE CHRISTOLOGICAL CLIMAX OF THE PERICOPE.** Matthew alone specifies the cloud as *phōteinē* (luminous / bright) — Mark and Luke have only *nephelē*. The *epeskiasen* (overshadowed) verb deliberately echoes LXX Exod 40:35 (the Sinai tabernacle-cloud) and the *episkiasei soi* of Luke 1:35 (the angel to Mary). **CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL**: the voice's wording — *Houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa* — is verbatim the Matthean baptism-voice formula at Mt 3:17 (Mark 1:11 and Luke 3:22 vary slightly), with the added imperative *akouete autou* (listen to him). The added imperative is itself a deliberate quotation of LXX Deut 18:15 *autou akousesthe* (the prophet-like-Moses passage — Moses commanding Israel to listen to the future prophet). This is a triple-layered allusion: (i) baptism-voice; (ii) Ps 2:7 royal-enthronement *huios mou ei sy*; (iii) Isa 42:1 servant-song *ho agapētos mou … en hō eudokēsen hē psychē mou*; (iv) Deut 18:15 prophet-like-Moses *akouete*. Davies-Allison ICC 2.706-707; Luz Hermeneia 2.402-405. **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: the canon engages the voice-from-cloud as an Elohim-communication-event paralleling the Sinai-cloud-voice (Exod 19:9) and the baptism-voice (Mt 3:17) — a recurring 'Elohim-broadcast' motif. **LENS-RISK FLAG for the Editor**: do NOT pre-resolve. Preserve the textual voice-from-luminous-cloud as Mosaic-Sinai typology + Davidic-royal acclamation + Isaian-servant identification + Deuteronomic-prophet-injunction. The four-layered allusion is the philological point; the metaphysical claim is the lens-question.

verses.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.
verses.translit: kai akousantes hoi mathētai epesan epi prosōpon autōn kai ephobēthēsan sphodra.
verses.notes: Matthew-only addition (not in Mark or Luke). The prostration *epesan epi prosōpon autōn* (fell on their face) is the LXX-standard theophanic-fear response (Gen 17:3 Abraham; Num 16:22 Moses and Aaron; Ezek 1:28; 3:23; 43:3 etc.). *ephobēthēsan sphodra* (were exceedingly afraid) — the *phobos*-of-theophany topos. Davies-Allison ICC 2.708.

verses.text: καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
verses.translit: kai prosēlthen ho Iēsous kai hapsamenos autōn eipen· Egerthēte kai mē phobeisthe.
verses.notes: Matthew-only addition. The touch + 'fear not' formula echoes the angelophanic-reassurance pattern (Dan 8:18; 10:9-10, 18-19 LXX; cf. Rev 1:17). *Egerthēte* (rise up) — the same verb (*egeirō*) that will be used of the resurrection (Mt 28:6 *ēgerthē*); deliberate Matthean foreshadowing.

verses.text: ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον.
verses.translit: eparantes de tous ophthalmous autōn oudena eidon ei mē auton Iēsoun monon.
verses.notes: The vision-closure: Moses and Elijah are gone; only Jesus remains. *auton Iēsoun monon* — the emphatic 'Jesus alone' marks the christological resolution: the Law (Moses) and the Prophets (Elijah) recede, leaving the Son who is to be heard (v.5). Davies-Allison ICC 2.708.

verses.text: καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ.
verses.translit: kai katabainontōn autōn ek tou orous eneteilato autois ho Iēsous legōn· Mēdeni eipēte to horama heōs hou ho huios tou anthrōpou ek nekrōn egerthē.
verses.notes: **THE 'TELL NO ONE' INJUNCTION**. *horama* (vision) — Matthew's distinctive term (Mark 9:9 has *ha eidon*); *horama* is the LXX technical term for prophetic vision (Dan 7:1 LXX; 8:1 LXX). The 'messianic secret' motif (Wrede 1901) reaches its Matthean climax here: the disclosure of the Son's glory must wait until the resurrection-event (*ek nekrōn egerthē*) which alone provides the interpretive frame. **CROSS-CORPUS to Mt 28:6** (the resurrection-announcement). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the canon-reading construes the silence-injunction as 'do not disclose the Elohim-engineering of the messenger until after the resurrection-demonstration' — flag for Editor disavowal; preserve text.

verses.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
verses.translit: kai epērōtēsan auton hoi mathētai legontes· Ti oun hoi grammateis legousin hoti Ēlian dei elthein prōton;
verses.notes: **ELIJAH-FIRST PERICOPE OPENING (vv.10-13)**. The disciples raise the standard 1st-c. Jewish-eschatological expectation: Mal 4:5-6 [MT 3:23-24] — Elijah-before-the-day-of-the-Lord. The scribal interpretation of this passage (Sirach 48:10-11; m. Eduyot 8:7; Justin Dial. 8.4, 49) is what's at issue. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 2.711-713.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα·
verses.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ēlias men erchetai kai apokatastēsei panta·
verses.notes: Jesus's affirmation of the scribal Elijah-tradition — *apokatastēsei panta* (will restore all things) echoes LXX Mal 4:6 [3:23] *apokatastēsei kardian patros pros huion*. The verb *apokatastasis* (restoration) is theologically loaded — picked up by later Christian universalism (Acts 3:21; Origen). The present *erchetai* may be construed as gnomic ('Elijah comes') or as still-future.

verses.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἠλίας ἤδη ἦλθεν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν ἀλλὰ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν· οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ' αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: legō de hymin hoti Ēlias ēdē ēlthen, kai ouk epegnōsan auton alla epoiēsan en autō hosa ēthelēsan· houtōs kai ho huios tou anthrōpou mellei paschein hyp' autōn.
verses.notes: The identification — Elijah has already come, suffered rejection (cf. John the Baptist's beheading at Mt 14:1-12), and the Son of Man will suffer parallel rejection. The typological linkage Elijah-John : Elijah's-rejection : Son-of-Man's-rejection is the structural point. Davies-Allison ICC 2.713-715.

verses.text: τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: tote synēkan hoi mathētai hoti peri Iōannou tou baptistou eipen autois.
verses.notes: Matthew-only explicit identification — Mark 9:13 leaves the inference to the reader. Matthean editorial clarification: Elijah-already-come = John-the-Baptist. **CROSS-CORPUS to Mt 11:14** (*autos estin Ēlias ho mellōn erchesthai* — 'he is Elijah who is to come').

verses.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν
verses.translit: Kai elthontōn pros ton ochlon prosēlthen autō anthrōpos gonypetōn auton
verses.notes: **DEMONIAC-BOY PERICOPE OPENING (vv.14-21)**. *gonypetōn* (kneeling) — a posture of supplication; the Matthean version compresses Mark's much-longer parallel (Mk 9:14-29) to about half-length, omitting the description of the crowd-dispute and the boy's specific symptoms. Davies-Allison ICC 2.717-720.

verses.text: καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν, ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς πάσχει· πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.
verses.translit: kai legōn· Kyrie, eleēson mou ton huion, hoti selēniazetai kai kakōs paschei· pollakis gar piptei eis to pyr kai pollakis eis to hydōr.
verses.notes: *selēniazetai* — literally 'is moon-struck' (from *selēnē*, moon); the ancient term for what modern medicine identifies as epilepsy (the symptoms of falling, convulsions, fire/water-danger). The lunar-influence etiology is the standard Greco-Roman folk-medicine framework (cf. Galen). Matthew uses *selēniazetai* only here and at 4:24; Mark and Luke have *pneuma alalon* (mute spirit) — Matthew has medicalized the Marcan demonological description but in v.18 still uses *daimonion* for the exorcism. The dual framing (medical + demonological) is itself a 1st-c. norm. Davies-Allison ICC 2.720-721.

verses.text: καὶ προσήνεγκα αὐτὸν τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν αὐτὸν θεραπεῦσαι.
verses.translit: kai prosēnegka auton tois mathētais sou, kai ouk ēdynēthēsan auton therapeusai.
verses.notes: The disciples' failure — set up for the faith-deficiency rebuke at v.20. The pattern (disciples' attempt → failure → Jesus's intervention → didactic-discourse on the failure) is the structural shape of the pericope.

verses.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε μεθ' ὑμῶν ἔσομαι; ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; φέρετέ μοι αὐτὸν ὧδε.
verses.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen· Ō genea apistos kai diestrammenē, heōs pote meth' hymōn esomai; heōs pote anexomai hymōn; pherete moi auton hōde.
verses.notes: The lament-exclamation *Ō genea apistos kai diestrammenē* directly echoes LXX Deut 32:5 (the Song of Moses — *genea skolia kai diestrammenē*). Matthew adds *apistos* (faithless) to the Deuteronomic *diestrammenē* (perverse / twisted) — the addition foregrounds the faith-deficiency theme of v.20. The Moses-typology (cf. v.5 *akouete autou* = Deut 18:15) continues.

verses.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον· καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
verses.translit: kai epetimēsen autō ho Iēsous, kai exēlthen ap' autou to daimonion· kai etherapeuthē ho pais apo tēs hōras ekeinēs.
verses.notes: Compressed exorcism — Matthew omits Mark's vivid convulsion-and-near-death detail (Mk 9:20-27). *epetimēsen* (rebuked) — the technical Matthean exorcism-verb (cf. 8:26 of the storm; 17:18 here). *apo tēs hōras ekeinēs* (from that hour) — Matthean signature instantaneous-healing formula (cf. 8:13; 9:22; 15:28).

verses.text: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ' ἰδίαν εἶπον· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
verses.translit: Tote proselthontes hoi mathētai tō Iēsou kat' idian eipon· Dia ti hēmeis ouk ēdynēthēmen ekbalein auto;
verses.notes: The private disciples-questioning *kat' idian* — same phrase as v.1 (the Transfiguration's private setting). The Matthean inclusio brackets the chapter's first half.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ, καὶ μεταβήσεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: ho de legei autois· Dia tēn oligopistian hymōn· amēn gar legō hymin, ean echēte pistin hōs kokkon sinapeōs, ereite tō orei toutō· Metaba enthen ekei, kai metabēsetai, kai ouden adynatēsei hymin.
verses.notes: **THE MUSTARD-SEED FAITH SAYING — CROSS-CORPUS to Mt 13:31-32** (the Parable of the Mustard Seed). The Matthean signature *oligopistia* (little-faith — Matthew-only NT word; cf. 6:30; 8:26; 14:31; 16:8) is here used substantively. *pistis hōs kokkos sinapeōs* — the smallest-seed-greatest-effect topos. *kai ouden adynatēsei hymin* (and nothing will be impossible for you) — echoes LXX Gen 18:14 (the Sarah-conception pronouncement) and Luke 1:37 (the annunciation). **HYPERBOLE-FUNCTION**: the mountain-moving image is the standard 1st-c. rabbinic hyperbole for the impossible (cf. b. Sanh. 24a). Davies-Allison ICC 2.728-730.

verses.text: [Τοῦτο δὲ τὸ γένος οὐκ ἐκπορεύεται εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ καὶ νηστείᾳ.]
verses.translit: [Touto de to genos ouk ekporeuetai ei mē en proseuchē kai nēsteia.]
verses.notes: **MAJOR TEXT-CRITICAL VARIANT — verse 21 is absent from the best witnesses**. Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, Codex Bezae (D), Coptic Sahidic, Old Latin (some), and Syriac Sinaiticus all omit. The verse is preserved in the Byzantine majority text and many later witnesses; it is a clear harmonizing assimilation from the Marcan parallel (Mk 9:29: *touto to genos en oudeni dynatai exelthein ei mē en proseuchē* — Mark itself has a variant *kai nēsteia* added in some witnesses). NA28, UBS5, SBLGNT, and THGNT all bracket or omit v.21. The KJV/TR includes it; modern critical translations omit or footnote. Preserved here in brackets per the data convention of recording the textual locus. Davies-Allison ICC 2.726 n.46; Metzger Textual Commentary 35.

verses.text: Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μέλλει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων,
verses.translit: Systrephomenōn de autōn en tē Galilaia eipen autois ho Iēsous· Mellei ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidosthai eis cheiras anthrōpōn,
verses.notes: **SECOND PASSION-PREDICTION** (after Mt 16:21; before Mt 20:18-19). The wordplay *huios tou anthrōpou … eis cheiras anthrōpōn* (the Son of Man into the hands of men) is deliberate paronomasia. *paradidosthai* (be handed over / be delivered up / be betrayed) — the same verb that will recur of Judas (Mt 26:15-16) and of the Father's delivering-up (cf. Rom 8:32). Variant: many witnesses read *anastrephomenōn* (returning / dwelling) for *systrephomenōn* (gathering together) — both are well-attested. SBLGNT and NA28 prefer *systrephomenōn*; THGNT prefers *anastrephomenōn*. Davies-Allison ICC 2.732-733.

verses.text: καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται. καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα.
verses.translit: kai apoktenousin auton, kai tē tritē hēmera egerthēsetai. kai elypēthēsan sphodra.
verses.notes: Completion of the passion-prediction with the third-day-resurrection formula (cf. Hos 6:2; 1 Cor 15:4 *kata tas graphas*). Matthean *tē tritē hēmera* differs from Mark's *meta treis hēmeras* (Mk 8:31; 9:31; 10:34) — the Matthean version conforms to the standard early-Christian credal formula. *elypēthēsan sphodra* (were exceedingly grieved) — Matthean addition (cf. v.6 *ephobēthēsan sphodra*); structural-emotion bookend within the chapter.

verses.text: Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ τὰ δίδραχμα;
verses.translit: Elthontōn de autōn eis Kapharnaoum prosēlthon hoi ta didrachma lambanontes tō Petrō kai eipan· Ho didaskalos hymōn ou telei ta didrachma;
verses.notes: **THE TEMPLE-TAX PERICOPE OPENING (vv.24-27) — Matthean SonderGut (Matthew-only material)**. *ta didrachma* (the two-drachma tax) — the half-shekel temple-tax mandated at Exod 30:11-16 (and at this period collected by the Jerusalem temple authorities; cf. Josephus *Ant.* 18.312; m. Shekalim). The pericope's dating-relevance: after 70 CE the Romans converted this tax into the *fiscus Judaicus* (paid to Jupiter Capitolinus instead of the temple — Josephus *War* 7.218). The pericope likely speaks to two contexts at once: (a) pre-70 temple-tax legitimacy; (b) post-70 *fiscus Judaicus* compliance. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 2.738-741; France NICNT 662-665; Bauckham, R., 'The Coin in the Fish's Mouth' (*Gospel Perspectives* 6, 1986).

verses.text: λέγει· Ναί. καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Τί σοι δοκεῖ, Σίμων; οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον; ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;
verses.translit: legei· Nai. kai elthonta eis tēn oikian proephthasen auton ho Iēsous legōn· Ti soi dokei, Simōn; hoi basileis tēs gēs apo tinōn lambanousin telē ē kēnson; apo tōn huiōn autōn ē apo tōn allotriōn;
verses.notes: *proephthasen* (anticipated) — implies Jesus's knowledge of the Petrine encounter outside the house, possibly thematic of prophetic foreknowledge. *telē ē kēnson* (customs or poll-tax) — the Latin *census* (poll-tax) is transliterated; this is a Roman-imperial-tax frame being analogically applied. The argument-from-royal-sons: kings tax foreigners, not their own sons — so the Son need not pay the Father's tax. Implicit christology + temple-as-Father's-house theology. Davies-Allison ICC 2.741-742.

verses.text: εἰπόντος δέ· Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρα γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί.
verses.translit: eipontos de· Apo tōn allotriōn, ephē autō ho Iēsous· Ara ge eleutheroi eisin hoi huioi.
verses.notes: The conclusion: the sons (= believers / Jesus + his followers) are *eleutheroi* (free) from the tax in principle. The implicit ecclesiological extension to all disciples (not just Jesus) is a Matthean concern at the post-70 redaction layer.

verses.text: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.
verses.translit: hina de mē skandalisōmen autous, poreutheis eis thalassan bale ankistron kai ton anabanta prōton ichthyn aron, kai anoixas to stoma autou heurēseis statēra· ekeinon labōn dos autois anti emou kai sou.
verses.notes: **THE COIN-IN-THE-FISH'S-MOUTH MIRACLE-PRINCIPLE PERICOPE-CLOSE**. Matthew-only material — no synoptic parallel. Note: the text describes the instruction but does NOT narrate the fulfillment; the reader is left to assume Peter executed it. *statēr* = a 4-drachma silver coin (= 1 shekel), sufficient for the two-drachma tax for two persons (Jesus + Peter). *skandalisōmen* (cause to stumble / give offense) — pragmatic-pastoral consideration overrides the principled freedom. Folkloric-parallels: the ring-in-the-fish topos (Herodotus 3.42 Polycrates of Samos; Augustine *De Civ. Dei* 22.8). The aphorism-form ('don't give offense') + miracle-image is the Matthean teaching-via-action signature. Davies-Allison ICC 2.745-749; France NICNT 666-667. **NO RAËLIAN-CANON ENGAGEMENT IDENTIFIED at this verse.**
